_comment: The first bundle in this repository whose every fact was read first-hand.
ADR 0015 says a fact enters a published bundle because somebody read it in
the game or in the publisher's own disclosure; ADR 0016 makes that
falsifiable. Until this file, no bundle here carried a first-hand fact —
the only publishable ones were synthetic fixtures declaring AUTHORED_FIXTURE.
Every number below is transcribed from
docs/game-facts/punishing-gray-raven-research-disclosure.md, which is the
reading itself. Nothing here was checked against a guide, a wiki or an
aggregator, deliberately: the cross-check is only worth something if it
happens after the authoring rather than during it.
It is small, and the smallness is the finding. What was read and could not
be written down is listed under 'what is missing and why' in the note; the
three that cost the most were the Themed Construct pool (PityRule.hardAt is
an int and PGR draws it uniformly 80-100 per cycle), the weapon Overclock
and Harmony recipes (read off a weapon whose name was not recorded, and an
Upgrade must name its entity), and the currencies (Item.rarity is required
and a currency is not graded on any screen that was read).
2026-09-19: the weapon was named (Hear the Bell), so its recipes are rows;
the fodder item was named; and the first stage and shop row landed. One
currency, Simulation Score, turned out to be graded on a screen after all.
Later the same day: Cogs and Phantom Pain Scar were graded on shop and
reward tiles too, and Helentine: Lacrimosa went in whole except Awaken,
whose tiers are conditions rather than costs. Still refused: the Themed
Construct pool, every level and rank gate whose level has no price (see
sequence 1 below), score-scaled weekly grants (see sequence 4 below), and the currencies no
screen has graded (Black and Rainbow Cards).
PGR records patches by name rather than number, so the label is a name.
Sequence 0 was published on 2026-09-19. Sequence 1 reads nothing new: it
writes down what sequence 0 had read and could not hold, now that an
upgrade can require a state and cost progress, and a fodder rule can say
which progress it pays. Her level to 80 (497 000 EXP), the Lv 80 gate on
her last Promote step, and the EXP halves of both Overclock rows.
Sequence 1 was published on 2026-09-19. Sequence 2 adds the Phantom Pain
shop's two shard rows, now that a shop limit can be one that never
resets: 10 shards at 10 Scars, then 20 at 20, 30 ever. The first tier is
the tile as read; the second is the maintainer's reading of the same tile.
Sequence 2 was published on 2026-09-19. Sequence 3 adds Samantha's
Upper Resonance, now that one step can have several prices (ADR 0021):
150 5-star Memory Shard, 234 Special Support Token or 246 Simulation
Score, any one of them. The Memory Shard was read only by its icon until
the maintainer opened its item card the same day.
Sequence 3 was published on 2026-09-19. Sequence 4 adds the weekly Phantom
Pain Cage, nine claim tiers and 56 Scars, now that a grant can stand behind
a score the reader supplies (ADR 0022). Nothing new was read: the tiles
were transcribed in the same 2026-09-19 sitting as the character and left
out because the format could only promise every reader the top tier. The
Scars they pay are the only source of the currency sequence 2's shard rows
spend, so Evolve to SS is a plan rather than a bill for a reader who says
what they clear.
Sequence 4 was published on 2026-09-20. Sequence 5 reads nothing new: it
writes down when this game's day starts, which was read on 2026-09-19 and
had nowhere to live. The home screen showed 00:04 server time while the
Resources menu counted down 04:58:18 to reset, and the server clock is UTC,
so the day rolls over at 05:00 UTC. Until now every game's weekday was read
in UTC at midnight, five hours early for this one (N20, ADR 0025).
It moves no plan in this file, because nothing here rotates by weekday: the
one stage is open every day. It is written anyway, because the first PGR
stage that does rotate would otherwise be farmed on a day that has not
begun and nothing would look wrong. One honest gap: a game-level field
carries no factProvenance row, exactly as energyUnit does not, so the fact
ledger cannot say that the reading behind this one is
'equipment-and-resource-screens'. This comment says it instead.
Sequence 5 was published on 2026-09-21. Sequence 6 prices the level
ladder and turns all twelve remaining Promote gates from prose into
requires: every step from 1 to 13 now names the level it needs, and this
file no longer holds a reading in a comment because the data could not
carry it. Read on 2026-09-21 off the Level Up preview, which reports the
level a selection would reach, so the twenty-two readings cost nothing
and levelled nobody.
The level track changes shape in the same sequence, from one row
level-1 -> level-80 into a thirteen-link chain. The total to Lv 80 is
unchanged at 497 000 and no published plan for Lv 80 alone moves. The
chain is what stops a plan wanting two gated levels paying the ladder
twice: DemandResolver walks backwards through fromState and skips rows it
has already counted, which spokes from level-1 would have defeated.
What this fixes is the partial plan. A reader going all the way to HERO
paid the ladder once either way; a reader stopping at Promote step 7 paid
Cogs and no EXP at all, because the level its screen demands was a
sentence in a comment. Now it is a demand.
The readings were taken on Luna: Oblivion rather than on Helentine:
Lacrimosa, and transferred on the maintainer's report that S-rank
constructs share a level curve. The report is cross-checked at three
points rather than assumed; the provenance entry says how.
Sequence 6 was published on 2026-09-21. Sequence 7 carries two changes
that have nothing to do with each other and one thing in common: each
was blocked on a field the format did not have.
N37. The three progress pools get names. A demand line for one has been
rendering as its bare slug — 'character-exp' beside a properly named
'Cogs' — since the first plan that demanded EXP, and there was no name
anywhere in the model to render instead. The names are at the foot of
this file and they are the only text here that was not read off a
screen: the game calls all three 'EXP' and naming them that way would
put three identical lines in one plan.
N28. The banner says what a pull costs: 250 Event Construct R&D Tickets
for one, 2 500 for ten, so no discount. That was read on 2026-09-18 in
the same sitting as the rates and has had nowhere to live since, because
a price names an Item and Item.rarity is required while no screen read
that year graded a currency. The ticket's tile was opened on 2026-09-22
and grades it five stars, which is the fourth currency read that way and
is what makes the price writable at all. IncomeModel — an interface with
no implementation for the whole of phase 5 — has one now.
What this does NOT do is move a plan. The solver does not pull, the
ticket is spent by nothing in this file, and no reward here grants one,
so DeclaredIncomeModel reads a balance and accrues zero. That gap is a
reading nobody has taken rather than a number anybody invented.
Sequence 8 corrects Lacrimosa's skills, and is the first sequence written
with a ladder (ADR 0031). Reading all four of her skill pages on
2026-09-24 found thirteen skills, eight on the level curve, where this
file had seven: 'Astral Armament' is on no page and is gone, and the
Signature Move (Allegory of the Wondrous Night) and the QTE (Fluid
Emotions) are added. A plan to every skill cap costs one skill more than
it did. The ladder itself moved nothing: written on its own, it diffed
against sequence 7 as no changes.
Sequence 9 puts Selena: Pianissimo and Lucia: Inverse Crown on the
S-rank ladder: a climber each, a shard each, and each shard's two
Phantom Pain shop rows. Every number is the ladder's, and what is theirs
is words, read off their skill pages and shard cards on 2026-09-24. The
two rows ADR 0031 held back for confirmation per climber, Evolve and the
SS passive's unlock, the maintainer confirmed for every S-rank construct.
Selena had been an entity since sequence 0, as the target of the Arrival
Construct pool, with nothing to climb; Lucia is new. She takes the place
Karenina: Effulgence had in the plan, because the maintainer does not
own Karenina and so cannot read her.
Sequence 10 changes no fact. It corrects which patch the readings were
taken on. The game moved from 4.7.0 "Steering By Light" to 4.8.0
"Anchored in Faith" at the 2026-09-24 maintenance, and every screen read
that day (Lacrimosa's skill pages, Selena's and Lucia's screens) was read
after it, where sequences 8 and 9 had called them "Steering By Light".
The label moves to 4.8.0 because that is the patch a reader plays. What
carries the 4.7.0 readings across is the maintainer's report of noticing
no cost change in 4.8.0, plus one point measured on both sides: a skill's
1 -> 2 at 1 Skill Point + 2 000 Cogs, read on 2026-09-19 and again on
2026-09-24. The file keeps its name; a file name is not a label.
Sequence 13 changes no fact and reads nothing: it gives the bundle's own
keys words a reader can read (ADR 0033), which D5's second rehearsal asked
for — the Cage's score, the item categories, the entity kinds. See 'words'.
Sequence 14 changes no number and reads nothing: every grade was written
'4*', an ASCII stand-in for the star the game draws, and D5's third
rehearsal read '6*' on the inventory as a typo. The 31 labels now say
'4★', as the item names in this file already did ('5★ Memory Shard').
The ranks are untouched, and the ranks are what every rule compares.

The pool screen carrying those panels is also where the price of a pull was read, on its own pull buttons: 250 Event Construct R&D Tickets for one and 2 500 for ten, so there is no ten-pull discount. That half was in front of the maintainer in the same sitting and had nowhere to live until sequence 7, which is why this detail line names it only now. The weapon Enhancement, Overclock and Harmony screens and the item detail cards behind them, same client, same patch, same account, same sitting. The Enhancement Cost picker was read with exactly one unit of fodder selected, which is where 'Obtained EXP 300' comes from.

The Select Equipment screen naming Hear the Bell (6-star, ATK 50 / CRIT 25, the same base stats the 2026-09-18 Enhance screen showed), the Weapon Enhancer IV item card, the Resources menu, the Simulated Battlefield stage screen and one run's Battle Results, the Simulation Score item card, the Simulation Shop's Material (both pages), Memory and Version Limited tabs, the reward screen from opening one stack of Overclock Material Box (beta), the Authority Level panel, and the Major Overclock Alloy, Weapon Overclock Core II and Memory Overclock Circuit II item cards. The Level Up screen's selection preview, read on Luna: Oblivion at Lv 1 / 80 — a freshly obtained S-rank construct, BP 326, no Memory equipped — with EXP Pods selected and the Level Up button never pressed, so the whole ladder was bracketed without spending anything. Twenty-two selections were read, and every one of the thirteen gated levels is pinned to a single multiple of 1 000 by the pair that brackets it — the total that reaches it and the total 1 000 lower that does not. 1 M (+1 000) shows Lv 10, and nothing smaller than one Pod exists, so Lv 2 and Lv 10 are both 1 000. Then: 3 M (+3 000) shows Lv 17 with 4 M (+4 000) showing Lv 20; 3 L (+9 000) shows Lv 29 with 3 L + 1 M (+10 000) showing Lv 30; 8 L (+24 000) shows Lv 39 with 8 L + 1 M (+25 000) showing Lv 40; 13 L (+39 000) shows Lv 44 with 13 L + 1 M (+40 000) showing Lv 45; 19 L + 2 M (+59 000) shows Lv 49 with 19 L + 3 M (+60 000) showing Lv 50; 29 L + 1 M (+88 000) shows Lv 54 with 29 L + 2 M (+89 000) showing Lv 55; 43 L (+129 000) shows Lv 59 with 43 L + 1 M (+130 000) showing Lv 60; 61 L + 2 M (+185 000) shows Lv 64 with 61 L + 3 M (+186 000) showing Lv 65; 87 L + 1 M (+262 000) shows Lv 69 with 87 L + 2 M (+263 000) showing Lv 70; 121 L + 1 M (+364 000) shows Lv 74 with 121 L + 2 M (+365 000) showing Lv 75; and 165 L + 1 M (+496 000) shows Lv 79 with 165 L + 2 M (+497 000) showing 80 / 80. The wider first brackets these replaced — 19 L, 29 L, 61 L, 87 L and 121 L, each 2 000 or 3 000 below its gate — were read in the same sitting and are superseded by the pairs above. Screenshots taken by the maintainer on 2026-09-21 and transcribed in a Claude Code session; not committed, because game assets are not allowed in this repository. Same client and account, patch 4.7.0 "Steering By Light". These figures are written on Helentine: Lacrimosa, not on Luna: Oblivion, on the maintainer's report that S-rank constructs share one level curve. That report is cross-checked rather than taken: the 2026-09-19 Lacrimosa readings of +1 000 -> Lv 10 and +3 000 -> Lv 17 are reproduced here exactly, and the (496 000, 497 000] bracket for Lv 80 is reproduced in both directions. Three agreement points, at both ends of the ladder. Luna: Oblivion is not an entity in this bundle, because she would arrive with a level track and no Promote, Skill or Evolve data. The screen's 'EXP 0/20' field is not recorded: it reads 0/20 at Lv 10, Lv 20 and Lv 80 alike, so it does not vary with level and cannot be a per-level requirement.

That she climbs the S-rank ladder — EXP per level, Cogs per Promote step, Skill Points and Cogs per skill level, 30 shards to Evolve S -> SS, 2 Skill Points + 20 000 Cogs for the SS passive's unlock — and that her shard's Phantom Pain shop tile is five stars and sells 30 ever, 10 at 10 Scars then 20 at 20, are the maintainer's reports of 2026-09-24 that these hold for every S-rank construct; none of those numbers was read on her screens. She replaces Karenina: Effulgence as the third construct on the ladder because the maintainer does not own Karenina. Screenshots taken by the maintainer on 2026-09-24 and sent to a Claude Code session; not committed, because game assets are not allowed in this repository. The maintainer's report of 2026-09-25, from playing, and NOT read off a screen in any sitting: every S-rank construct has an Ultima Awaken under Common Effect, it opens once the construct has been awakened four times, and unlocking it costs what the leader skill's unlock does (3 Skill Points and 25 000 Cogs). _comment: The Arrival Construct archetype, read on Selena: Pianissimo. Its sibling,
the Themed Construct archetype read on Karenina: Effulgence, is NOT here:
its guarantee is a value drawn uniformly between 80 and 100 and redrawn
on every S-Rank, and PityRule.hardAt is an int. Writing any one number
there would be inventing a rule the screen does not state.
Two further things on the same screen that the model has nowhere to put:
the guarantee is inherited by the next pool of the same type with a
pending Calibration included, where PityScope.BANNER_TYPE says only that
the bucket is the type; and the per-10 A-Rank-or-above floor is here but
both engines ignore floors below the headline by design.
No availability window: the dates 09/17 - 10/01 06:59 were read, the zone
they are in was not, and Availability takes instants. That is N20.
The stated overall S-Rank rate including the guarantee is 1.90%, which
does not reproduce from 0.50% and a wall at 60 (it computes 1.925%). The
note argues the 1.90% is a long-run outcome share rather than a per-pull
probability, which is why only the row the screen calls 'Base Drop' is
written as a base rate here.
One 4-star unit of weapon EXP fodder closes 300 EXP, read off the
Enhancement Cost picker with one unit selected. It reads 300 whether the
unit is an EXP material or a 4-star weapon, which is the single largest
simplification the reading produced: progressPerUnit is a function of the
fodder's rarity band alone.
The band is carried by consumesCategory rather than by minimumRarity,
because Fodder has no upper bound and the 5* / 4* / 1-3* filter buttons
on that screen imply the value moves with the band. Only the 4* figure
was read, so saying 'four stars and above give 300' would over-claim.
Weapon Enhancer IV carries that category since 2026-09-19, when its
name was read; before then the rule was inert rather than hung on an
invented item. The 4-star weapons the picker also offers are not items
here, so feeding a weapon is still outside the model.

_comment: Ultima Awaken, one per S-rank construct, written by hand rather than on
the ladder: a climber's sourcedBy beats a row's there (ADR 0031), so a
laddered row would be credited to Selena's and Lucia's screen sittings,
and this is not a screen reading at all. See ultima-awaken-report, which

It opens only after the fourth Awaken (maintainer). This bundle has no
Awaken track, so that is not a gate here: a gate must name a state some
step reaches, and a plan to unlock it does not count the awakenings it
stands behind. Its tag on the Common Effect page is unread, so it has
none, and the roster names it from its ids.
The S-rank construct ladder, written once (ADR 0031). Every row below is
expanded once per entity in appliesTo, its id prefixed with the entity's
and every {placeholder} replaced by that entity's own word, before the
bundle is parsed; the database, the diff and the planner see the same
per-construct rows this file held by hand until sequence 8.
Why it is shared: the maintainer reports, from levelling many constructs
and from opening Selena: Pianissimo's and Karenina: Effulgence's screens
beside Lacrimosa's on 2026-09-24, that every S-rank construct pays the
same EXP per level, the same Cogs per Promote step and the same Skill
Points and Cogs per skill level. The level curve was already read on a
second construct, Luna: Oblivion, on 2026-09-21. What differs per
construct is words: the shard Evolve spends, the SS passive's name and
the skills' names.
Since sequence 11 a row also says what the game calls things (ADR 0032):
a Promote state's rank and stars, and the heading and tag its track sits
under. They are text read off the same screens as the row's numbers, so
the row's provenance covers them. The rank of every state is her Promote
tab, read at each step from PRIVATE to HERO in character-screens and
again in the maintainer's screenshots of 2026-09-25, which show one panel
per state and as many star icons as the rank has states; the maintainer
confirmed that PRIVATE already shows its one star filled. The headings
and tags are her skill pages (skill-pages, 2026-09-24), which the
screenshots of 2026-09-25 show again; that the Leader skill sits first
under Common Effect is the maintainer's reading of that screen, where it
shows locked. That the layout is the same for every S-rank construct,
only the skills' names differing, is the maintainer's report of
2026-09-25. 'Growth' is the one word here the game does not show: Level,
Promote and Evolve have no shared heading in the client, and like the EXP
pools' names below it is this bundle's word for its own grouping.
Provenance: a row's sourcedBy says where its numbers were read, the
ladder's covers the rest, and a climber's sourcedBy, when it has one,
covers every row it expands to — that is the sitting which says the
numbers are also that construct's.
Promote, the whole ladder, read one Rank Up screen at a time up to HERO,
'Max Level Reached': thirteen steps, Cogs only, 542 500 in total.
States count steps; the ranks they cross are PRIVATE (step 1), SERGEANT
(2-3), ELITE (4-6), TASK FORCE (7-9) and ACE (10-13), ending at HERO.
Every step is also gated on a level — 2, 10, 20, 30, 40, 45, 50, 55, 60,
65, 70, 75, 80. Step 11's 'Lv.70' was read through the weapon model
overlapping the text; the sequence around it agrees.
Since sequence 1 an upgrade could require a state, and step 13 required
level-80. Since sequence 6 every step requires its level, because the
whole ladder is priced — the thirteen level rows are below. No gate in
this bundle is prose any more, and this comment no longer holds up a
reading the data cannot carry.
The rule that kept the other twelve out is worth keeping. DemandResolver
passes mustBeReachable = false for a gate, deliberately, because a gate
may name the start of a track, so a required state that no upgrade
produces resolves to an empty path and costs nothing. A gate naming a
level with no row reaching it is therefore met by every plan for free,
which is worse than prose: prose is honest about being unread, and a
free gate looks priced.
The level track, as a chain rather than as spokes from level-1. Every
figure is a cumulative reading from Lv 1 off the Level Up preview, and
the rows below carry the differences between consecutive ones. Nothing
here was levelled: the preview reports the level a selection would
reach, so the whole ladder is readable without spending a Pod.
The chain is what DemandResolver needs. It walks backwards through
fromState and sums every row it crosses, skipping any already counted,
so a plan wanting Lv 40 for one Promote step and Lv 80 for another pays
the ladder once. Thirteen rows each hanging off level-1 with a
cumulative figure would have charged it twice.
No Cog cost shows on Level Up and the maintainer confirms none.
Every Pod is a multiple of 1 000 and the smallest, EXP Pod (M), is
1 000, so a figure is 'exact as a demand in Pods' when no smaller
multiple of 1 000 reaches the level — which is the only sense in which
a plan can be short of EXP. The true EXP thresholds between multiples
are unread and unreadable from this screen; for Lv 2 the true figure is
certainly far below 1 000, and 1 000 is still the honest demand,
because nothing smaller can be spent.
Readings, all from Lv 1, each gate pinned by the pair that brackets it
— the total that reaches it and the one 1 000 lower that does not:
1 M (1 000) reaches Lv 10, and nothing smaller than one Pod exists;
3 M (3 000) reaches Lv 17 and 4 M (4 000) reaches Lv 20;
3 L (9 000) reaches Lv 29 and 3 L + 1 M (10 000) reaches Lv 30;
8 L (24 000) reaches Lv 39 and 8 L + 1 M (25 000) reaches Lv 40;
13 L (39 000) reaches Lv 44 and 13 L + 1 M (40 000) reaches Lv 45;
19 L + 2 M (59 000) reaches Lv 49 and 19 L + 3 M (60 000) reaches Lv 50;
29 L + 1 M (88 000) reaches Lv 54 and 29 L + 2 M (89 000) reaches Lv 55;
43 L (129 000) reaches Lv 59 and 43 L + 1 M (130 000) reaches Lv 60;
61 L + 2 M (185 000) reaches Lv 64 and 61 L + 3 M (186 000) reaches Lv 65;
87 L + 1 M (262 000) reaches Lv 69 and 87 L + 2 M (263 000) reaches Lv 70;
121 L + 1 M (364 000) reaches Lv 74 and 121 L + 2 M (365 000) reaches Lv 75;
165 L + 1 M (496 000) reaches Lv 79 and 165 L + 2 M (497 000) reaches
So the cumulative EXP from Lv 1 is 1 000, 1 000, 4 000, 10 000,
497 000 for the thirteen gated levels, and the rows below carry the
differences. Every one is a single multiple of 1 000 with the multiple
below it observed to fall short, so none is a bound or a guess.
Five of them were first bracketed 2 000 or 3 000 wide, because a Pod
(L) is 3 000 and the crossing was made by adding whole Pods (M) to a
run of them; one more selection each closed them. All five turned out
to sit at the top of their range, which is what an upper bound would
have assumed — and it is written here because it was read, not because
it was assumed.
The 2026-09-19 Lacrimosa reading of one EXP Pod (XL), +20 000 ->
Lv 37, is not reproduced here but sits strictly between 10 000 -> Lv 30
and 24 000 -> Lv 39, so the two readings do not contradict.
Lv 2 and Lv 10 are both 1 000: one Pod (M) is the smallest spendable
amount and it already carries a construct to Lv 10, so no Pod purchase
distinguishes them. The level-2 -> level-10 row is therefore free, and
that is a reading rather than a hole — the state exists, the chain
crosses it, and the step costs nothing. A gate naming a state with no
row at all is the hole, and is what the nine unpriced levels avoid by
staying prose.
The last link, 365 000 to 497 000. Sequence 1's figure of 497 000 was
this row's whole cumulative, read as one step from Lv 1; 132 000 is
the same reading expressed as the end of a chain that now names every
gated level between.

three pools 'EXP' — the character Level Up screen reads EXP 0/20, the

EXP 300' — so the game's own words would put three lines reading 'EXP'

'character-exp' is one, and they carry no factProvenance row for the
same reason the energy unit and the day boundary carry none.
A kind with no name renders as its slug, which is what sequences 0 to 6
do and go on doing: they are published and immutable.
